Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me, I really appreciate it. 

Um... well, I'm here because of a... a bit of a situation at work. It's honestly a little embarrassing to talk about, but I want to be completely cooperative. I work in human resources, and recently I sort of... pushed ahead with a new onboarding launch. I was just trying to be proactive, you know? But I guess I committed some company money and vendor time before all the official approvals were completely in place. 

At the time, it honestly felt like exactly what the department needed—it felt bold and necessary to just get it done. I thought I was doing a good job. Does that make sense? But... well, now they've placed me on leave, and everyone is asking what I was thinking. I just want to figure this out so I can get back to being a reliable employee, if that's okay?
Can you tell me if there have been times in your life when you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or were more talkative than usual for several days at a time?

Um... unusually energetic? I mean, I guess I have moments where I feel pretty productive, you know? Like when I was working on that onboarding project, I was definitely focused and getting a lot done. But... I don't know if I'd call it "unusual." Isn't it normal to feel a little extra motivated sometimes when you're passionate about a project? 

As for sleep... maybe I was sleeping a little less around that time, just because I wanted to get things finished. But I didn't feel exhausted or anything, so I figured it was fine. And talkative... well, I am in HR, so I talk to people all day anyway. I might have been a bit more enthusiastic than normal, but... I don't think it was anything too crazy. I hope that answers your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Can you recall if there was a time when your mood was unusually high, euphoric, or irritable for several days in a row, where you felt like you didn’t need sleep or were more impulsive than usual?

Um... unusually high or euphoric? I mean, I guess over the past few weeks, I did feel... well, I felt really good. Like, brilliantly alive, honestly. I just had this strong sense that I could finally show leadership what our HR department could really be, you know? It felt like a really positive thing at the time. I hope it doesn't sound arrogant to say that. 

But... well, I suppose there were moments where I might have been a little irritable, too. It wasn't anything major, I don't think! Just... if someone questioned me, even over really small things like routine budget questions or minor edits to the onboarding materials, I'd get... suddenly really frustrated. Almost furious, which isn't like me at all. I usually pride myself on being very even-tempered at work. I know I probably shouldn't have reacted that way, and I feel terrible if I made anyone uncomfortable. Does that sound like what you're asking about, doctor? I really want to be as helpful as possible here.

Can you tell me if there was a time when your mood was elevated or irritable most of the day, nearly every day, for at least several days in a row — not just momentary shifts, but a sustained change in how you were feeling internally?

Um... a sustained change? Most of the day, every day? I mean... I don't think so? I don't want to mislead you, but I don't really remember feeling like that constantly. 

I mean, sure, I had those moments of feeling really great about the project, and maybe those flashes of frustration I mentioned... but it wasn't like I was just walking around angry or, or overly ecstatic every single minute of the day for a week straight. I still did my normal routine, you know? I still went to meetings and answered emails and did the regular HR stuff. I don't think my internal mood was completely altered the whole time. 

I'm sorry, I hope I'm understanding the question right. I just wouldn't say it was a constant, all-day thing. Is that... is that okay? I'm trying to be as accurate as I can for you.

Can you tell me if there was a specific period of time—lasting several days or more—when you felt a noticeable increase in your energy or drive to get things done, beyond what you’d consider your normal, even outside of work projects?

Um... an increase in energy? I mean, I suppose I have been a lot more... active lately. But I honestly just thought of it as being really dedicated to my role, you know? Like, I've been getting into the office quite early, before everyone else, and... well, I guess I've been walking the floors a lot. And I've been doing a ton of rewriting—going over presentation decks, sending out emails, rearranging plans. 

It actually felt really productive! Though... I will admit, maybe it was a bit intense. It got to the point where sitting still at my normal desk felt... almost impossible? Like, I don't know, like my body just had this motor in it and I just had to keep moving to get it all done. I hope that doesn't sound too strange or... or out of control? I just really wanted to make sure I was staying on top of everything for the team. Is that the kind of thing you're looking for? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

Can you tell me if there was a specific period lasting at least 4 or 5 days in a row when your mood was clearly different from usual—like feeling unusually upbeat, high, or irritable much of the time, even if it wasn't constant every minute?

Um... well, if you mean just generally different from my usual self for a stretch of time... I guess, yes? I mean, like I mentioned, for the past few weeks, I've had these stretches where I just felt brilliantly alive. Like I finally had the clarity to show leadership what HR can really be, you know? It felt like such a positive, productive mindset to be in. I really hope that doesn't come across as me being full of myself or anything. 

But then... yeah, there were those other times during these same few weeks. The times I'd get suddenly furious if someone questioned me. And looking back, it was over such trivial things, like small edits to a document or routine budget questions. I'm usually so good at taking feedback, so getting that angry... it's not a good look for me, I know. I feel awful about it. So, yes, I suppose for the last few weeks my mood has been sort of bouncing between those two extremes. Does that help clarify things? I really hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.

While bipolar I disorder (F31.13) remains a differential, the interview does not confirm a history of more than one manic episode or a prior major depressive episode, which are required for that diagnosis.
